## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Fóshuō Sì-tiānwáng jīng* (T590) is a one-fascicle short sūtra translated jointly by Zhìyán 智嚴 ([智嚴](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%BA%E5%9A%B4)) and Bǎoyún 寶雲 ([寶雲](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%AF%B6%E9%9B%B2)) under the Liú-Sòng 劉宋. The Buddha explains the function of the *cāturmahārāja* — the four great kings of the Heaven of the Four Mahārājas (Vaiśravaṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Virūḍhaka, Virūpākṣa) — as protectors of the Dharma who tour the world on the eighth, fourteenth, and fifteenth of each lunar month to inspect human merit.

**Abstract**

A short cosmographical-monitory sūtra explaining the role of the Four Mahārājas as moral overseers; a key textual source for the East Asian "six fast-days" (六齋日) lay-observance system. Translation precisely datable to 427 CE on the *Chū sānzàng jì jí* evidence.
